language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I am Scotty! My family and I are taking a vacation. We are flying from Miami, Florida, where we live, to Bermuda, then to San Juan, Puerto Rico. From San Juan we fly back home to Miami.

Bermuda and Puerto Rico are surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean. Both islands and Florida too have sub-tropical to tropical climates. That means the temperature ranges from warm to hot and it is almost always very humid.

The route we are taking forms a triangle, known as the Bermuda Triangle, where planes and ships have mysteriously disappeared. But we're not
going to disappear!

Hi, I am Scotty! My family and I are taking a vacation. We are flying from Miami, Florida, where we live, to Bermuda, then to San Juan, Puerto Rico. From San Juan we fly back home to Miami.

Bermuda and Puerto Rico are surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean. Both islands and Florida too have sub-tropical to tropical climates. That means the temperature ranges from warm to hot and it is almost always very humid.

The route we are taking forms a triangle, known as the Bermuda Triangle, where planes and ships have mysteriously disappeared. But we're not
going to disappear!
While I am flying to each destination, I am going to do some extra credit work for school. My science teacher gave me a workbook to complete.
I have to figure out how energy is transferred between organisms. Photosynthesis is the process by which plants make food.
The substance made by plants during photosynthesis is starch. Starch gives the plant energy. And, starch gives humans energy, too!
In school, we experimented with iodine and saw that different food items contained starch.

When starch was present, the iodine changed from brown to blue-black
or purple.
This was due to a chemical reaction. Let’s see if you can help me remember which foods contained starch.

In this section of my workbook, I have to complete the food chains for all the types of habitats, like oceans and forests. Food chains show how each living thing gets its food. Some animals eat plants and some animals eat other animals. Each link in the food chain is eaten by the next link. The only exception is the organism that stands on top of the entire chain.

Do you think you can help me complete some of these food chains? Just drag the animals to their correct spot in the
food chain.

This section of my workbook is all about building food pyramids. A food pyramid shows all the food relationships of different organisms with similar feeding styles. Inside a pyramid you can create an entire food chain from producer all the way to the top predator.
